kings2.6.p1.b1.text: Please take note that the place where we meet with you is too small for us. Please let us go to the Jordan, where each of us can get a log so we can build ourselves a place to live there.

kings2.6.p1.b4.text: So Elisha went with them, and when they came to the Jordan, they began to cut down some trees.

kings2.6.p2.b1.text: Oh, my master, … it was borrowed!

kings2.6.p2.b3.text: The man of God cut a stick, threw it there, and made the iron float.

kings2.6.p3.b1.text: My camp will be in such and such a place.

kings2.6.p3.b2.text: Then the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: “Be careful passing by this place, for the Arameans are going down there.”

kings2.6.p3.b3.text: Tell me, which one of us is on the side of the king of Israel?

kings2.6.p3.b4.text: No one, my lord the king. For Elisha, the prophet in Israel, tells the king of Israel the very words you speak in your bedroom.

kings2.6.p4.b1.text: Go and see where he is, that I may send men to capture him.

kings2.6.p4.b2.text: When the servant of the man of God got up and went out early in the morning, an army with horses and chariots had surrounded the city.

kings2.6.p4.b3.text: Oh, my master, what are we to do?

kings2.6.p4.b4.text: Do not be afraid, … for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.

kings2.6.p5.b1.text: O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see.

kings2.6.p5.b2.text: And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw that the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

kings2.6.p6.b1.text: Please strike these people with blindness.

kings2.6.p6.b2.text: This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are seeking.

kings2.6.p6.b3.text: Then the LORD opened their eyes, and they looked around and discovered that they were in Samaria.

kings2.6.p7.b1.text: My father, shall I kill them? Shall I kill them?

kings2.6.p7.b2.text: Do not kill them, … Set food and water before them, that they may eat and drink and then return to their master.

kings2.6.p7.b3.text: So the king prepared a great feast for them, and after they had finished eating and drinking, he sent them away, and they returned to their master.

kings2.6.p7.b4.text: And the Aramean raiders did not come into the land of Israel again.

kings2.6.p8.b1.text: So there was a great famine in Samaria. Indeed, they besieged the city so long that a donkey’s head sold for eighty shekels of silver …

kings2.6.p8.b2.text: Help me, my lord the king!

kings2.6.p8.b3.text: If the LORD does not help you, where can I find help for you? From the threshing floor or the winepress?

kings2.6.p8.b4.text: This woman said to me, ‘Give up your son, that we may eat him, and tomorrow we will eat my son.’ … But she had hidden her son.

kings2.6.p9.b1.text: When the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes. … the people saw the sackcloth under his clothes next to his skin.

kings2.6.p9.b2.text: May God punish me, and ever so severely, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on his shoulders through this day!

kings2.6.p9.b3.text: Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door to keep him out. Is not the sound of his master’s footsteps behind him?

kings2.6.p9.b4.text: This calamity is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?
